compete = to take part in a race or contest and try to win
opponent = the person or team you play against
referee = the official who controls a football or rugby match
umpire = the official who controls tennis or volleyball
stadium = a large building with seats around a sports field
pitch = the grass area where football or rugby is played
court = the marked area for tennis, basketball or volleyball
track = the path used for running races
goalkeeper = the player who stops the ball going into the goal
score = to get a goal or point; the number of points
draw = a result where both sides have the same score
defeat = a loss; to win against someone
victory = the fact of winning
championship = a competition to decide the best team or player
tournament = a series of games until there is a winner
athlete = a person who is trained for sport, especially running or jumping
coach = a person who trains a team or player
training = regular practice to get better at a sport
warm-up = gentle exercise before a hard session
injury = damage to your body from sport or an accident
spectator = a person who watches a sports event
supporter = a person who regularly follows a team
take up = to start doing a sport or hobby regularly
give up = to stop doing something you used to do
keep fit = to stay healthy through exercise
individual sport = a sport you do alone, not in a team
team sport = a sport played by groups against each other
extreme sports = sports with a high level of danger, such as climbing
martial arts = sports such as karate or judo
gymnastics = exercises on the floor or apparatus that need strength and control
athletics = sports that include running, jumping and throwing
swimming pool = a place with water for swimming
changing room = a room where you change clothes before sport
trophy = a cup or object given to the winner
medal = a metal disc given for first, second or third place
break a record = to do better than the best result so far
football = a game of two teams who kick a ball into a goal
basketball = a game where you throw a ball through a high hoop
volleyball = a game where two teams hit a ball over a net with their hands
handball = a team game where you throw a ball into a goal
tennis = a game where you hit a ball over a net with a racket
table tennis = a game like tennis played on a table with small bats
badminton = a game where you hit a shuttlecock over a net
squash = a fast indoor game hitting a ball against a wall
hockey = a team game played with sticks and a small ball
ice hockey = a fast team game on ice with sticks and a puck
rugby = a team game with an oval ball that you can carry
cricket = a bat-and-ball game that is popular in England
baseball = an American bat-and-ball game with four bases
golf = a game where you hit a small ball into holes with clubs
skiing = moving over snow on long thin boards
snowboarding = moving over snow on one wide board
ice skating = moving on ice wearing boots with blades
roller skating = moving on wheels attached to your shoes
skateboarding = riding a short board with wheels
cycling = riding a bicycle as sport or exercise
running = moving fast on foot as sport
jogging = running slowly for exercise
swimming = moving through water using your arms and legs
diving = jumping into water head first, or swimming underwater
sailing = travelling on water in a boat with sails
rowing = moving a boat with oars
kayaking = paddling a small closed boat
surfing = riding waves on a board
climbing = going up rocks or a wall using your hands and feet
hiking = long walks in the countryside as a sport or hobby
horse riding = sitting on a horse and controlling it
boxing = a sport of fighting with the fists in gloves
wrestling = a sport of holding and throwing an opponent
judo = a Japanese martial art of throws and holds
karate = a martial art of kicks and punches
yoga = exercises for the body and breathing
aerobics = fast exercises to music that make you breathe harder
fitness = how healthy and strong your body is
workout = a session of physical exercise
stretch = to make muscles longer and more flexible
cool-down = gentle exercise after sport so your body slows down
stamina = the ability to keep exercising for a long time
strength = how much force your muscles can use
flexible = able to bend your body easily
out of breath = breathing hard because you have exercised
personal best = your own fastest or best result ever
race = a competition to see who is fastest
sprint = a very short, fast race
marathon = a running race of about 42 kilometres
relay = a race where team members run one after another
hurdles = a race where you jump over barriers
long jump = an athletics event of jumping as far as you can
high jump = an athletics event of jumping over a bar
shot put = throwing a heavy metal ball as far as you can
javelin = a long spear thrown in athletics
penalty = a free shot at goal after a serious foul
foul = breaking the rules by hitting or holding someone
offside = a football rule about being too far forward
kick-off = the first kick that starts a football match
half-time = the break in the middle of a match
extra time = more playing time when a knockout match is a draw
penalty shoot-out = taking turns at penalties to decide a drawn match
own goal = when you accidentally score for the other team
hat-trick = three goals by the same player in one match
captain = the player who leads the team on the field
substitute = a player who comes on for someone else
bench = the seats for players who are not on the field
kit = the clothes a team wears for a match
strip = a team's match colours and shirt design
football boots = special shoes for football or rugby
shin pads = plastic guards that protect your lower legs
helmet = a hard hat that protects your head
goggles = protective glasses for swimming or skiing
racket = the thing you use to hit the ball in tennis or badminton
bat = a wooden stick used to hit the ball in cricket or table tennis
net = the mesh that divides a court or is a goal in some sports
goal = the frame you score into; a point scored that way
whistle = the object a referee blows to stop or start play
scoreboard = the board that shows the score
league = a group of clubs that play each other over a season
cup final = the last match of a knockout competition
semi-final = a match whose winner goes to the final
qualifier = a match you must win to enter a bigger competition
Olympic Games = the world's biggest multi-sport event, every four years
World Cup = an international tournament to find the best national team
home game = a match played at your own stadium
away game = a match played at the other team's stadium
season ticket holder = a fan who has paid for all home matches
fair play = playing by the rules and showing respect
doping = using banned drugs to improve sport results
disabled sport = sport organised for athletes with disabilities
PE kit = the clothes you must wear for physical education
